statement: Genomic analysis of a high-coverage Neanderthal genome from the Altai Mountains estimates the population divergence between the Neanderthal/Denisovan ancestral lineage and the Homo sapiens lineage at approximately 550,000-765,000 years ago — a genetic model estimate, distinct from and often conflated with the much younger fossil date range of classic Neanderthal specimens themselves (see claim_sima_de_los_huesos_earliest and claim_neanderthal_extinction_date). Other calibrations and models produce somewhat different ranges.

sources.citation: Prüfer, K. et al. "The complete genome sequence of a Neanderthal from the Altai Mountains." Nature 505: 43-49.
sources.author: Prüfer et al.

notes: Confidence set to MODERATE rather than HIGH because the reporting agent noted other calibrations/mutation-rate models give somewhat different divergence ranges; this is a model-dependent estimate, not a direct observation.
